channel.title: Kyunolab Mystery Archive
channel.description: Legends, folklore, mysteries, and strange tales.

item.title: Tunguska Event Mystery: Siberian Blast, Flattened Forest, and the Explosion Without a Crater
item.description: The Tunguska event remains one of the clearest examples of a real historical mystery: a vast Siberian blast, a flattened forest, eyewitness reports, scientific surveys, and no ordinary impact crater.

item.title: Flannan Isles Lighthouse Mystery: Missing Keepers, Empty Station, and the Sea Record That Stayed Open
item.description: The Flannan Isles lighthouse mystery follows the disappearance of three keepers from a remote Scottish lighthouse and the unsettling gap between official record, sea weather, and legend.

item.title: Trojan Horse Legend: Hidden Soldiers, Wooden Gift, and the Object That Opened a City
item.description: The Trojan Horse legend follows the wooden gift that entered Troy, the hidden soldiers associated with it, and the lasting warning about victory disguised as surrender.

item.title: Mjolnir: Returning Weapon, Thunder Sign, and the Object That Carries Protection
item.description: Mjolnir is followed as a Norse mythic object: a returning thunder weapon, a protective sign, and a compact symbol whose meaning reaches beyond battle.

item.title: Mount Olympus: Greek Divine Home, Clouded Summit, and the Place Where Gods Look Down
item.description: Mount Olympus is remembered as the mythic home of the Greek gods, a high place where weather, power, distance, and divine politics gathered above the human world.

item.title: Valhalla: Odin Hall, Chosen Warriors, and the Norse Place Waiting for Battle Again
item.description: Valhalla is remembered as Odin's hall for chosen warriors, a Norse afterlife image where battle, honor, death, feast, and final destiny meet.

item.title: Bioluminescent Bay Phenomenon: Glowing Water, Tiny Organisms, and the Shore That Lights Up at Night
item.description: Bioluminescent bays are real glowing-water phenomena where tiny organisms, darkness, motion, and sheltered coastal conditions make the shoreline seem to light from within.

item.title: Catatumbo Lightning: Lake Maracaibo Storms, Night Flashes, and the Sky That Keeps Returning
item.description: Catatumbo lightning is remembered for frequent night flashes near Lake Maracaibo, where geography, storms, and local memory turned weather into a recurring natural spectacle.

item.title: Tantalus Punishment Myth: Forbidden Feast, Water, Fruit, and Desire Kept Just Out of Reach
item.description: The punishment of Tantalus is remembered as a Greek myth of forbidden closeness: water below, fruit above, desire everywhere, and relief always out of reach.

item.title: Sisyphus and the Boulder: Endless Labor, Divine Punishment, and the Hill That Never Ends
item.description: Sisyphus and the boulder is remembered as a Greek myth of endless labor, divine punishment, repetition, cleverness, and the hill that refuses completion.

item.title: Basilisk: Deadly Gaze, Serpent King, and the Creature Small Enough to Terrify a Bestiary
item.description: Basilisk is a pre-existing Mythic Creatures subject built around the legendary serpent-like creature remembered through deadly gaze, poisonous breath, rooster associations, and medieval bestiary tradition.

item.title: Draugr Folklore: Restless Dead, Barrow Fear, and the Body That Would Not Stay Buried
item.description: Draugr is a pre-existing Mythic Creatures subject built around the Norse undead figure remembered through burial mounds, physical danger, haunting presence, and saga tradition.

item.title: Okiku Doll Legend: Growing Hair, Temple Display, and the Japanese Doll People Kept Watching
item.description: Okiku Doll is a pre-existing Modern Legends subject built around the Japanese haunted-doll legend associated with hair said to grow, temple display, family memory, and later paranormal retellings.

item.title: Crying Boy Painting Urban Legend: House Fires, Newspaper Panic, and the Picture That Survived
item.description: Crying Boy Painting is a pre-existing Urban Legends subject built around the British urban legend that reproductions of a crying child painting survived house fires and became treated as cursed objects.

item.title: Spring-Heeled Jack: Leaping Attacks, Victorian Panic, and the Figure That Would Not Stay Human
item.description: Spring-Heeled Jack is a pre-existing Modern Legends subject built around the Victorian legend of a leaping attacker remembered through sensational reports, strange physical details, and urban fear.

item.title: Green Children of Woolpit: Strange Visitors, Green Skin, and the Medieval Story of Another Country
item.description: Green Children of Woolpit is a pre-existing Classic Folklore subject built around the medieval English account of two green-skinned children said to have appeared near Woolpit and described a strange homeland.

item.title: Dancing Plague of 1518: Strasbourg Records, Exhaustion, and the Mystery of a Public Frenzy
item.description: Dancing Plague of 1518 is a pre-existing Unexplained Mysteries subject built around the Strasbourg event remembered through reports of people dancing for days, public anxiety, medical explanation, and unresolved interpretation.

item.title: Why Salt Is Used for Protection in Folklore: Purity, Thresholds, and the Line Danger Should Not Cross
item.description: Salt Protection Folklore is a pre-existing Legend Origins subject built around the repeated folklore pattern that uses salt as a sign of purity, preservation, boundary-making, and protection at thresholds.

item.title: Why Knocking on Wood Became Good Luck: Trees, Touch, and the Habit of Protecting a Hope
item.description: Knocking on Wood is a pre-existing Legend Origins subject built around the superstition pattern in which touching or knocking on wood protects a wish, reverses a boast, or calls on older tree symbolism.

item.title: Lemuria: Lost Continent Theory, Occult Geography, and the World That Moved From Science to Legend
item.description: Lemuria is a pre-existing Lost Worlds subject built around the lost-continent idea that began as a scientific hypothesis and later moved into occult geography, mythic speculation, and popular legend.
